title: Horizontal pasting for compactification-relative constant and strict-tower exchanges
statement:
Let $B$ be a commutative ring. For each scheme $T$ use the small pro-etale site and constant-$B$ module derived operations [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations]. Work either in $D(T_{\mathrm{proet}},\underline B_T)$ or in $D(\mathcal T_T)$, where $\mathcal T_T=\operatorname{Fun}(\mathbf N_{\geq1}^{\mathrm{op}},\operatorname{Mod}(\underline B_T))$, with the normalized termwise derived adjunctions and compositors of [def-cbc-strict-constant-tower-operations]. Let $f:X\to Y$ be separated of finite type and supply a compactification $c=(j:X\hookrightarrow\overline X,p:\overline X\to Y)$ with $j$ quasi-compact open and $p$ proper [def-weil-compactifications-refinements]. Let $a:Y_1\to Y$ and $b:Y_2\to Y_1$ be arbitrary scheme maps and use their pullback compactifications [pur713-def-base-changed-compactification], identifying $(c_a)_b$ with $c_{a\circ b}$ by the unique projection-preserving fibre-product isomorphism [def-pc-fibre-product]. Write $a_X,b_X,\bar a,\bar b$ for the induced maps on opens and compactifications, $A_t$ for inverse image, $P=Rp_*$, $P_a=Rp_{a,*}$ and $J=j_!$; in the tower case these symbols mean the derived termwise operations and termwise open extension [def-cbc-strict-tower-open-extension]. Let $E_a:A_aP\to P_aA_{\bar a}$ be the unit--square--counit mate [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate], and $\beta_a:A_{\bar a}J\xrightarrow{\sim}J_aA_{a_X}$ the open-unit-normalized comparison [lem-cbc-strict-tower-proper-open-calculus]. Set $H_a=(P_a\beta_a)\circ(E_aJ)$, and define $E_b,\beta_b,H_b$ on $c_a$ in the same way. Then, with the canonical pullback compositors,
$$E_{a\circ b}=(E_bA_{\bar a})\circ(A_bE_a),\qquad
\beta_{a\circ b}=(\beta_bA_{a_X})\circ(A_{\bar b}\beta_a),$$
$$H_{a\circ b}=(H_bA_{a_X})\circ(A_bH_a).$$
These are natural-transformation equalities for the specified derived maps; in the tower case they hold before evaluation. For finite $B$, evaluation of the tower maps agrees with the ordinary constant-$B$ maps. When $B=A_{E,n}$ and the schemes and base maps satisfy the finite-coefficient hypotheses of [def-exchange-projection], these ordinary maps are exactly its chosen-compactification maps. The equations respect the projection-preserving identifications for three successive base maps, independently of parenthesization. No etale-origin hypothesis, isomorphism hypothesis on the base maps, or equivariant compactification is required.

proof.text: Identify the iterated base-changed factorizations with the one for $a\circ b$. Both iterated fibre products represent triples with the same projection equations. The two comparison maps preserving those projections are inverse by uniqueness. This also identifies the open maps, since their maps into the compactification are uniquely characterized by the two projection equations. For three base maps both bracketings preserve every projection, so the comparison is the same. These are precisely the identifications used below.

proof.text: Evaluation commutes with the exact tower pullbacks and open extensions by localization of their termwise squares. For direct image use the existing evalR comparison, the mate of evalG inverse, which is invertible by K-injective evaluation. Apply the coefficient-exchange counit theorem to the evaluated pullback square to identify E. Use beta_evaluation for beta, after identifying ordinaryBeta with singleBeta by localization and inversion of the same module transpose. Expand supportEval and H; naturality of evalR and ordinaryE combines the two equations. These are direct equations of specified maps; no faithfulness of evaluation is asserted or used.

proof.text: Apply strict pullback-square pasting to the inverse square comparisons. Invert the isomorphisms to obtain the forward-square pasting equation. For any three adjunctions, cancel the right compositor, transpose through the final adjunction, and apply the mate counit formula twice. Naturality of the second square, the forward-square equation and naturality of the right compositor give the pasted proper-mate equality. The same argument proves the ordinary assertion. For ordinary pullbacks, descend the associative section-normalized module compositors by exact localization; normalization of a square by the two compositors gives the same pullback-square pasting calculation. All base maps remain arbitrary.

proof.text: Use beta_comp from the strict proper/open calculus for the tower open comparison. For ordinary modules first prove that the extension-by-zero adjunction unit is invertible: compare with the localized-site open adjunction through the fully faithful fixed-coefficient restriction functors. The cartesian module square identifies the target with an object in the fully faithful open extension image, so the counit and the transposed pulled-back unit are invertible. Localize its unit equation. Transpose successive inverse beta maps through the three open adjunctions and apply the ordinary square-pasting equation. Inverting this equality gives ordinary beta pasting. Cancellation uses only beta and the specified pullback compositors, never a proper exchange map.

proof.text:
Suppress the canonical compositors and evaluate on an arbitrary object $K$ of the derived tower category. Expanding the two $H$ factors gives
$$P_{ab}(\beta_{b,A_{a_X}K})\ E_{b,J_aA_{a_X}K}\ A_b(P_a(\beta_{a,K}))\ A_b(E_{a,JK}).$$
Naturality of $E_b:A_bP_a\to P_{ab}A_{\bar b}$ at the morphism $\beta_{a,K}:A_{\bar a}JK\to J_aA_{a_X}K$ replaces the middle two factors by $P_{ab}(A_{\bar b}\beta_{a,K})\ E_{b,A_{\bar a}JK}$. Functoriality, Step 4 and Step 3 now make the result $P_{ab}(\beta_{ab,K})E_{ab,JK}=H_{ab,K}$. The calculation is natural in $K$, proving the transformation equality before evaluation. The identical naturality calculation combines the separately proved ordinary factors. Only naturality and functor composition were used; no $E$ or base map was inverted.

proof.text: Apply the two-step pasting equations to the first two squares, the last two squares, and the two resulting pairs. Quasi-compactness of the intermediate open follows by cartesian base change. Replace each nested paste with its single composite map. The two parenthesizations of each scheme composite are equal by category associativity; equality elimination identifies their exchange, beta and H maps, including precisely the displayed eqToHom factors. Proof irrelevance identifies the supplied commutativity witnesses.

proof.text: For the quotient coefficient ring use its recorded finiteness. The canonical derived compositor, transported to constantRingIso for the composite, has its specified normalized adjunctions, direct-image section formula, module conjugate and termwise complex comparison. The canonical adjunction unit theorem identifies those adjunctions with the actual module adjunctions. The section formula uniquely identifies the direct-image compositor with moduleRComp. Conjugation identifies the module compositor with moduleGComp, and exact localization identifies the derived compositor with ordinaryGComp. This is the general normalized-comparison localization calculation exposed by the existing comparison-localization module. Hence sourceSquare equals the ordinary square. ordinaryBeta and singleBeta are the same localization of the inverse open-unit transpose. Substitute these two equalities into compactificationExchangeFromData; its definition is exactly ordinaryH, including the associators. Specialize to the literal base-changed compactification on the unchanged finite-type S domain.
